title: A 1982 pulse makes the radiation transition duration uncertain in five-member ECHAM6.3 SST contrasts
abstract: We tested immediate and gradual radiation changes at the November 1981 SST source switch in five-member ECHAM6.3 AMIPII and HadISST1 ensembles. We fit calendar-year averages of fixed-date transitions lasting zero to 20 years over 1950-2016. An immediate step fits best with a constant or a linear time term. With a separate 1982 pulse, a 17-year ramp fits slightly better. Its residual loss difference from the immediate step is -0.047 W2 m-4, with member-bootstrap limits -0.248 to +0.154. The immediate shape is selected in 30.2% of member draws with the pulse, against 90.5% without it. The long-period radiation decrease remains clear. Thus these annual data do not uniquely select an immediate lasting step when a short pulse is allowed. The result limits a physical interpretation of step removal; it does not refute the dataset effect or establish a slow atmospheric response. One model, five members, simple transition shapes, nuisance assumptions and annual global means limit inference. We supply code, exact source provenance, shape profiles, window tests and all resampling statistics.

display.caption: Annual radiation contrast and residual loss profiles for fixed-date transition shapes. Pulse control allows a distinct 1982 response. Shape ranking depends on this choice.

citations.reason: Uses its ECHAM6.3 annual ensembles and tests the immediate-step interpretation against gradual shapes with a separate pulse.
Motivates separating the 1982 transient from the lasting response; the present study uses different ensemble data.
